evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-1997-006
evidence.claim: The bonding and earthing step was made mandatory in 1997 following a static spark incident during acetone transfer.
evidence.quote: Reason: static spark during acetone transfer (NM-1997-004).

evidence.title: Compliance memo CM-2004-011 - hazardous areas, solvent handling
evidence.claim: In 2004, the bonding step in SOP-07 was confirmed as a legal requirement for flammable liquid transfers.
evidence.quote: SOP-07 bonding step confirmed as a legal requirement.

evidence.title: NEAR-MISS REPORT NM-1997-004
evidence.claim: A static spark occurred in August 1997 during acetone transfer from a drum to tank T-5 due to electrical isolation.
evidence.quote: the operator saw a spark at the drum bung when the transfer nozzle touched it

evidence.title: INCIDENT REPORT IR-2001-007
evidence.claim: A flash fire occurred in 2001 during white spirit transfer, likely caused by static discharge from a PVC hose.
evidence.quote: White spirit vapour ignited, probable static discharge from the PVC transfer hose.

evidence.title: INCIDENT REPORT IR-2001-007
evidence.claim: A 2001 flash fire during white spirit transfer was caused by flammable vapors and PVC hoses, reinforcing the need for static control.
evidence.quote: Root cause: white spirit flash point is about 38 °C; at 58 °C the batch was well above it

evidence.title: CHANGE REQUEST CR-2001-012
evidence.claim: A 2001 flash fire during white spirit letdown into a hot batch reinforced the need for antistatic measures.
evidence.quote: Reason: flash fire IR-2001-007 - letdown of white spirit (flash point approx. 38 °C) into a hot batch.

evidence.title: Safety data sheet (extract) - White spirit D40
evidence.claim: As of 2022, the safety data sheet for White spirit D40 still requires precautionary measures against static discharge.
evidence.quote: take precautionary measures against static discharge

verdict.process_name: SOP-07 solvent cleaning of dispersers and mixing vessels
verdict.instruction: Bond and earth the vessel and the solvent drum before any solvent transfer.
verdict.reason: The step was mandated after a 1997 static spark incident (E1, E3) and is a legal requirement for flammable liquid transfers (E2). Subsequent incidents in 2001 (E4, E5, E6) and 2022 SDS requirements (E7) confirm the hazard of static discharge during solvent transfer remains present.
